description: A 3-track audio looper with its own clock, metronome click, pre-roll and two stereo main outputs

params.text: Resets the beat counter, so the next clock counts as a bar clock
Sets the tempo of the internal clock, 30.0 to 300.0 BPM; changing it does not stretch loops already recorded
Sets the time signature, from 2/4 up to 15/8, which sets how many clocks make a bar
Sends the metronome click to the EAR output
Sets the level of the click, 0 to 200%
Sends the click to the MASTER output as well as the EAR output
Counts a bar or two of click in before the tracks start, but only when every track is stopped
Chooses whether the pre-roll counts one bar or two
Starts every recorded track, or stops them all if any one is playing, recording or overdubbing; with a cable in the ALL STOP jack this only starts
Sets the level of the EAR output, 0% to 100%
Sets the level of the MASTER output, 0% to 100%
Sets the level of that source, 0 to 200%, with the centre at 100%
Silences that source; it has to be off before anything can be recorded from it
Chooses which source that track records from
Sets how many bars that track's loop lasts, 1 to 16
Ties that track to the clock, so a command takes effect on the next bar; with it off the track starts and stops at once and its MEAS knob is ignored for recording
Starts that track from the position the bar has already reached, instead of waiting for the loop to come round
Stops that track at once with an 8ms fade, instead of waiting for the loop to end
Puts that track in the solo group, where only one track at a time plays, records or overdubs; it can only be changed while the track is empty or idle
Plays, records or overdubs that track's loop once and then leaves it idle
Plays or overdubs that track's loop backwards; the direction changes only when the loop reaches its end
Sets that track's crossfade between the end of a loop and its restart, 0 to 1000ms; it comes up at 8ms
Pans that track's own stereo output; the main outputs and what is recorded are not panned
Sets the level of that track's output, 0% to 100%
Starts recording on that track if it is empty, or overdubbing if it already holds a loop
Starts playback of that track's loop; the PLAY Button Sequence menu item changes what repeated presses do
Stops playback, recording or overdubbing on that track
Double-click to erase that track's loop; it only works while the track is idle
Sends that source straight to that track's own outputs as well

inputs.text: The left channel of that source; with nothing in the right jack this one is used for both
The right channel of that source
A trigger here does what that track's REC button does
A trigger here does what that track's PLAY button does
A trigger here does what that track's STOP button does
A trigger here erases that track's loop
An external clock to follow instead of the internal one; with a cable here the clock is treated as always running
A trigger here does what the STRT/STOP button does
A trigger here stops every track, and leaves the STRT/STOP jack free to start them

outputs.text: The left channel of that track's output
The right channel of that track's output
A 1ms pulse when that track's loop reaches its end, and on a forced stop when 'EOL pulse on stop' is ticked
A 1ms pulse on every clock, generated or received
The left channel of the EAR output, meant for headphones, which always carries the click when it is on
The right channel of the EAR output, meant for headphones, which always carries the click when it is on
The left channel of the MASTER output, meant for speakers
The right channel of the MASTER output, meant for speakers

notes: nothing is recorded until a source's MUTE button is off and something is connected to it; the level is set with that source's LVL knob while you test it.
a loop is recorded for an extra second past its end, the recording tail, and the XFD crossfade is taken from that tail.
an imported loop has no recording tail, which is what the 'Extra samples Tail (1sec)' setting on the track menu is for.
the PLAY and REC lights show the state: both off is empty, PLAY lit steady is idle, PLAY flashing is playing, REC flashing is recording, both flashing is overdubbing.
a fast flash on PLAY or REC means a command has been given and takes effect at the end of the loop; pressing the same button again cancels it.
each track's vertical bar shows the position in the loop and its colour shows the state: black empty, red first recording, blue idle, green playing, yellow overdubbing.
right-clicking a track's bar display opens that track's menu: Fade IN on playback, Play Full Tail on Stop, Import Wav, Export Wav, Extra samples Tail (1sec), Detect tempo and set bpm.
the track outputs carry the same signal that also reaches the main outputs, so patching both sends a track twice.
menu: SOURCEs to MASTER out — sends every source to the MASTER output; with it off that output carries only track playback
Only Click on EAR — sends only the click to the EAR output, and nothing else
EOL pulse on stop — sends a pulse from a track's EoL output when its loop is forced to stop as well as at its natural end
PLAY Button Sequence — sets what the PLAY button and its jack do: start and stop, or record then play then overdub, or record then overdub then play, with STOP the only way out of the last two
Instant STOP button — makes the STOP button drop a track to idle at once, except during the first recording of a synced track
OVERDUB after REC — moves a track into overdub by itself at the end of its first recording
Tracks settings — opens the same items each track's bar display carries, from the module's own menu
Load preset (+loops) — reads a .slp file of every setting, and the loop wav files beside it when they are there
Save preset — writes a .slp file of every setting
Save preset + loops — writes a .slp file of every setting and each recorded loop as its own wav file
Internal Clock Always ON — keeps the internal clock running even with every track idle, as an external clock does
Click Settings — a submenu choosing between the three built-in click pairs, or loading a wav file for the beat click and another for the bar click
